transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Vela, Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Vela, Eng Manager), Anya Petrova (Vela, Cloud Architect)

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, seein' some people pop in, we'll give it a sec. this call is to scope the POC for cost modeling and run the benchmarks.
[00:12] Priya Shah: sounds good, thanks. quick context, we're trying to decide between running in our VPC vs Redwood hosted, and cost is a huge factor, so we want to get per-token estimates and understand batching/caching tradeoffs.
[00:26] Liam O'Connor: great. quick intro from our side — i'm Liam, infra SE, i'll run the bench and help with runtime knobs. main outputs: a cost model spreadsheet, benchmark results (latencies, throughput, tokens), and recommended config (batching, cache TTL, quantization profile).
[00:45] Marcus Lee: we have some constraints: many short chat-like prompts (average 120 tokens in, 30 tokens out) but also occasional long inferences (2–3k tokens). Peak concurrency is about 200 concurrent users with bursts up to 500. monthly token budget target is ~$1.5M tokens but will scale.
[01:12] Anya Petrova: security is important — we need VPC peering or private deployment, KMS integration, and audit logs. SOC2 is ok but we need details.
[01:28] Sofia Martinez: totally — we'll share SOC2/ISO docs and our VPC runbook. for the cost model: do you want hosted math with burst credits, or pricing for dedicated pooled GPUs?
[01:40] Priya Shah: we want both: quick hosted estimate for a pilot and the dedicated numbers if we go enterprise. need to know per-token server-side cost after batching/caching.
[01:52] Liam O'Connor: ok, to make that concrete, we'll estimate cost per effective token = (GPU cost / effective throughput) + infra margin. effective throughput depends a lot on batch size, concurrency, prefix caching hit-rate, and average sequence length.
[02:12] Marcus Lee: can you show example calcs?
[02:18] Liam O'Connor: sure — rough numbers: on a T4-like pool or an A10 equivalent, a single GPU can do ~15k tokens/s for short seqs with aggressive batching. but that's very workload dependent. with continuous batching and a 32-token avg output, your per-token cost could be $0.00001–0.00005 on hosted; on dedicated the unit cost drops but ops + reserved commit changes the math. again, approximate.
[02:48] Priya Shah: sorry just to clarify — when you say tokens/s is that decoded or both directions?
[02:55] Liam O'Connor: decoded tokens (generation). encode/decode both count; usually we charge per input+output token. in the spreadsheet we'll split I/O tokens and show examples.
[03:10] Sofia Martinez: i'd also like to highlight savings from prefix/KV caching — if you have lots of repeated system prompts or shared history, you can see 20–60% effective token reduction for some chat patterns.
[03:25] Priya Shah: interesting, our UX does reuse system prompts a lot. do you have TTL knobs?
[03:31] Liam O'Connor: yes — cache TTL and KV cache sharding are configurable. in POC we'll test hit rates; typical configs are 5–30 minutes for session caches, and a permanent shared prefix cache for templates.
[03:45] Marcus Lee: on latency — our SLO is p95 < 200ms for <256 token inferences and p99 < 300ms. is that realistic?
[03:55] Liam O'Connor: for hosted with our low-latency routing and optimized kernels it's possible in many cases, but it depends on queuing (batching) and network hops. with dedicated GPUs colocated in your region and small batch windows you can hit p99 ~200–250ms for short prompts. for longer contexts it rises. we'll include latency vs throughput curves in the benchmark.
[04:21] Sofia Martinez: ok let's capture success criteria verbally: 1) p99 latency for short prompts < 300ms, 2) stability under 200 concurrent users for 24h load with acceptable tail latency, 3) per-token cost <= $0.00005 for hosted pilot or clear path to $0.00002 on dedicated at commit levels. agree?
[04:41] Priya Shah: that sounds reasonable as a starting point.
[04:44] Anya Petrova: on security checklist, we also need SAML SSO, RBAC mapping, KMS, and VPC egress rules. can you provide a runbook?
[04:55] Sofia Martinez: yes, we'll attach our VPC runbook and SSO/KMS integrations doc.
[05:02] Marcus Lee: about benchmarks — we want a representative prompt set. we'll share 200 sample prompts including chat flows and long inference cases.
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: perfect. plan for benchmarking: 1) ingest your prompt set and profile token lengths; 2) run synthetic traffic with your concurrency/peak patterns for 72 hours (or three 24h runs); 3) capture p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, GPU utilization, batching stats, cache hit rate; 4) produce per-token cost under different batch sizes and cache hit assumptions.
[05:36] Priya Shah: what's the benchmark environment? hosted or a dedicated bench cluster?
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: we'll do both: hosted sandbox first, then a dedicated-sized instance that matches expected production. dedicated run will use quantized model variant if applicable (we'll propose Q4/8-bit profile).
[05:54] Priya Shah: can you explain how batching window impacts latency vs cost? we want knobs we can tune.
[06:00] Liam O'Connor: short: larger batch windows increase GPU throughput (lower per-token cost) but add queuing latency. we can control max batch size and wait-time (e.g., 10ms wait to collect batch vs 50ms) and the runtime will trade off latency. for chat workloads with many small messages, small wait windows + prefix caching usually win.
[06:22] Sofia Martinez: we'll include a sensitivity table in the spreadsheet: batch wait 5/20/50ms and batch size limits 8/32/128 and corresponding cost/latency.
[06:32] Marcus Lee: about quantization — we are okay with some quality loss if it reduces cost 30–50%. can you recommend profiles?
[06:38] Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll run A100/3090-like and 8-bit quant variants; we'll surface any quality regressions in evaluation scores vs your expected outputs. recommended starting points: LLM-2-medium Q4 for balanced quality, Q8 if budget-tight for dedicated.
[06:56] Priya Shah: curious about caching effectiveness — what's realistic hit rate?
[07:02] Liam O'Connor: depends — per-user session caches are small helps (10–30% for chat sessions). shared prefix caches for templated prompts can hit 40–60% for some flows. in POC we'll measure with your prompt set.
[07:18] Anya Petrova: networking — if we go private, what's the connection model? VPC peering or private link?
[07:24] Sofia Martinez: both supported; we prefer PrivateLink for minimal routing but VPC peering is common for on-prem setups. we'll send exact steps.
[07:34] Priya Shah: timeline — we want to decide by end of October. what's realistic?
[07:39] Sofia Martinez: POC plan: week 0 (this week) gather prompts + access; week 1 run hosted benchmarks; week 2 run dedicated benchmarks and quant tests; week 3 analyze results and iterate; week 4 finalize cost model and recommendations. so ~4 weeks.
[08:00] Marcus Lee: OK. for cost model inputs, here's what we'll provide: typical convo length distribution, peak concurrency windows, and expected monthly token volume.
[08:10] Sofia Martinez: great. we'll also provide an excel with pre-filled assumptions and formulas: GPU$/hour, expected tokens/sec per GPU for each model variant, batching efficiency factor, cache hit assumptions, and ops markup.
[08:22] Priya Shah: what about billing granularity — can you provide both per-token and per-1000-token projections?
[08:27] Sofia Martinez: yes we'll show per-token, per-1k tokens, and monthly burn scenarios.
[08:32] Liam O'Connor: quick note: the effective per-token observed in benchmark = raw per-token * (1 - cache_hit) / batching_efficiency. we'll show that formula in the sheet.
[08:44] Priya Shah: if we see quality regressions when quantizing, we might accept higher cost. need to see delta in evaluation.
[08:50] Liam O'Connor: agreed, we'll attach automated evals on the output set comparing baseline FP32 and quant variants and flag regressions.
[08:58] Marcus Lee: any constraints around data retention/logs? we need audit logging and optional log purge policy.
[09:04] Sofia Martinez: yes, we support configurable retention; logs can be sent to your SIEM or stored for X days. we'll include that in security docs.
[09:12] Priya Shah: what's a realistic pilot cost to run the benchmark? we have a small budget for this POC.
[09:18] Liam O'Connor: for a 3-day hosted bench at the scale you described (50k tokens/day baseline), raw infra might be a few hundred to low thousands depending on concurrency. we'll provide an estimate in the spreadsheet; the main value is the per-token curves that let you extrapolate.
[09:35] Anya Petrova: any blockers from our side? we'll need a service account and egress rules updated for the benchmark runner.
[09:42] Sofia Martinez: noted. Priya/Anya, can you create a temp service account with minimal scopes and add our IPs? we'll send the IP range.
[09:50] Priya Shah: yes i'll get that by Thursday.
[09:54] Marcus Lee: last Q — do you support model pinning and automatic fallback if a dedicated pool is saturated?
[09:59] Liam O'Connor: yes, routing policies allow pinning to model versions and automatic fallback to compatible variants (e.g., quantized or smaller architecture) to preserve availability. we'll demo that in the follow-up if useful.
[10:12] Sofia Martinez: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: we'll send cost-model spreadsheet + VPC/SSO docs; Vela will share prompt set and create service account; Liam will schedule benchmarks and run them; follow-up week of 9/21 to review results.
[10:30] Priya Shah: thanks everyone.
[10:32] Marcus Lee: thanks.
[10:33] Anya Petrova: bye.
